clues.title: Plate: short white, blue strip
text: Finland has shorter than normal **white** plates with the standard European **blue strip** on the left.
NOTE: Åland has small, [fully white plates](https://goo.gl/maps/UoGQEzJqUPbe5bWX7) with blue lettering.
clues.summary: Shorter than normal white plates with the usual blue strip on the left.

differs.how: Åland plates are short, fully white, no blue strip

clues.title: Road lines: edge lines always solid white
text: Where present, outer road lines will always be **solid white lines**.
NOTE: Unlike Sweden and Norway, Finland does not use dashed outside lines. The only exception to this are the Åland Islands in southwest Finland, which do use dashes.
clues.summary: Where there are edge lines, they are always solid white. Sweden and Norway use dashed edge lines. Only the Åland islands in the southwest use dashes.

differs.how: Sweden uses dashed edge lines
Norway uses dashed edge lines
Åland uses dashed edge lines

clues.title: Road lines: white dashes or yellow centre lines
text: Finland has several different types of **middle road lines**, including:
- [white dashes](https://goo.gl/maps/yQ7mJwXhJez2CDKa6), with or without a solid white line next to it
- [solid yellow with white dashes](https://goo.gl/maps/USv1DEYbXfne7ZsVA)
- [double yellow](https://goo.gl/maps/U3WZ4fLRZUEjuZFp8).
Yellow lines are being phased out and are increasingly rare in newer coverage.
NOTE: Sweden never has yellow middle lines. Norway has middle lines that have a distinct [orange tint](https://goo.gl/maps/pBepFW6otTJTFaDn6).
clues.summary: Centre lines can be white dashes (with or without a solid line), solid yellow with white dashes, or double yellow. Yellow is being phased out. Sweden never has yellow centre lines.

differs.how: never has yellow centre lines
centre lines have an orange tint

clues.title: Bollard: black and white, long, diagonal stripe
text: Finland has **long black-and-white bollards** with a rectangular, white reflector on the front and two dots on the back. They can be either round or thin and curved. The black strip is typically diagonal.
NOTE: They can look somewhat similar to bollards found in other Northern European countries. [This infographic](/images/finland/nordics_bollards.png) shows the differences.

images.caption: Black-and-white bollards in tall grass, each circled in red with an arrow to the small bollard it magnifies

clues.summary: Long black and white bollards with a rectangular white reflector on the front and two dots on the back. Round or thin and curved, with a usually diagonal black stripe. Other Nordic bollards look similar.

clues.title: Pole: orange snow pole, thin white band at top
text: In Finland, it is common to find **orange snow poles** with a thin white band near the top.

NOTE: These are also found commonly in Norway and Sweden, but with a much [wider white band](https://i.imgur.com/R8PSzB4.png?1), lower down on the pole. They can also have multiple white bands, while Finnish snow poles usually have just one band.

images.caption: A red arrow points to the thin white band at the top of an orange snow pole
A red arrow points to the thin white band at the top of an orange snow pole
Two orange snow poles with a double arrow, labelled Se and NO for Sweden and Norway

clues.summary: Orange snow poles with one thin white band near the top. Norway and Sweden have them too, but with a much wider white band lower down, sometimes several bands.

differs.how: wider white band, lower, sometimes several bands
wider white band, lower, sometimes several bands

clues.title: Language: long words, double vowels, ä and ö
text: The **Finnish language** is not related to most other European languages, so it has a very unique look. It has a lot of long words and double vowels. The Finnish alphabet includes the letters **ä** and **ö**.
NOTE: Estonian is closely related to Finnish, so it can look similar. Estonian uses the letters õ and ü, which are not used in Finnish.

images.caption: Finnish text with Ä and Ö shown large

clues.summary: Unrelated to most European languages, with many long words and double vowels, and the letters ä and ö. Estonian looks similar but uses õ and ü, which Finnish lacks.

clues.title: Street sign: white with black text, ends in tie or katu
text: Most Finnish street names end in “**tie**” or “**katu**.” These are the Finnish words for road and street. Street signs most commonly have a white background with black text.
NOTE: You may find roads ending in “polku” and “kuja”.
clues.summary: Street names mostly end in 'tie' (road) or 'katu' (street), on white signs with black text. 'Polku' and 'kuja' also appear.

clues.title: Sign: yellow background road signs
text: Finnish road signs have a **yellow background**.
NOTE: Signs in Sweden and Iceland also have yellow backgrounds. Norway, however, has signs with a white background.
clues.summary: Road signs have a yellow background. Sweden and Iceland do too, but Norway's are white.

differs.how: Norwegian signs have a white background

clues.title: Sign: thin yellow edge on red-border signs
text: On traffic signs that have a red border, you will find a thin **yellow stroke** on the edge of the sign.
NOTE: You will not see this in any other Nordic country.

images.caption: Circle zooms in on the thin yellow edge of a red-bordered warning sign, top right

clues.summary: Traffic signs with a red border have a thin yellow stroke on the very edge. No other Nordic country has this.

clues.title: Sign: pedestrian sign with 5 stripes
text: Finnish pedestrian signs have **5 stripes**.
NOTE: Pedestrian signs in Sweden and Norway **usually** have 4 stripes. In [rare cases](https://goo.gl/maps/wMS7W2CWGyAi4DJt9), you can find 5 stripes in Norway.
clues.summary: The pedestrian sign has 5 stripes. Sweden and Norway usually have 4, though Norway rarely has 5.

differs.how: usually 4 stripes
usually 4 stripes, rarely 5

clues.title: Sign: solid blue direction sign, white border
text: Finnish **directional signs** consist of a solid blue background, white text, and a white border with guiding arrows.
clues.summary: Direction signs are solid blue with white text and a white border, with arrows.

clues.title: Chevron: black with yellow arrows
text: Finnish chevrons are **black with yellow arrows**.
NOTE: Norway and Iceland have similarly coloured chevrons. Sweden, on the other hand, has unique blue and yellow chevrons.
clues.summary: Chevrons are black with yellow arrows. Norway and Iceland use similar colours, but Sweden has blue and yellow ones.

differs.how: Swedish chevrons are blue and yellow

clues.title: Pole: simple wooden poles, often with a street light
text: Finland primarily uses **wooden utility poles**. Most of them tend to have a simple design, but they can have a variety of poletops. Poles often have a street light attached to them.
NOTE: In Northern Europe, wooden poles are also common in Sweden, Norway, and Estonia.
clues.summary: Mostly wooden utility poles with simple designs but various tops, often with a street light attached. Sweden, Norway and Estonia use wooden poles too.

clues.title: Pole: lamp bolted twice at the very top
text: Lamps attached to wooden poles in Finland are normally mounted to the **top **of the pole with a **double bolting**.

NOTE: Within Scandinavia, [Sweden](https://maps.app.goo.gl/B38WAHnBB6minmXg9) also uses double bolting. However, in Sweden the lamps are mounted further down and the lamp arms are usually not straight.
clues.summary: Lamps on wooden poles are mounted on top with a double bolt and a straight arm. Sweden also double-bolts, but lower down and usually with curved arms.

differs.how: lamps lower on pole, arms usually not straight

clues.title: Sign: blue and white striped signposts
text: Traffic signposts often have **blue and white** striped markings.

NOTE: This pattern can also be found in Sweden. While the same colour scheme is also common in [Estonia](https://www.google.com/maps/@58.3430383,26.7407475,3a,22.2y,264.88h,67.51t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1sP587UApP9JnjyawxVML4YA!2e0!7i13312!8i6656), the markings typically have a wider shape and attach to the signpost in a looser way.
clues.summary: Signposts often have blue and white stripes. Sweden has this too. Estonia has the same colours, but its stripes are wider and attached more loosely.

differs.how: stripes wider, attached looser to the post

clues.title: Landscape: dense forest of pine and birch
text: Most of Finland is covered by dense **boreal forests**. Pine trees are common, as well as birches, which are easily recognizable by their white trunks.
clues.summary: Dense boreal forest. Pines are common, plus birches with white trunks.

clues.title: Google car: Gen 3 coverage in autumn colours
text: A lot of **Generation 3** coverage was taken in **autumn**, meaning that trees in this coverage often have distinct fall colours.

NOTE: This is significantly less common in Generation 3 coverage in the other Nordics. This means that when you are faced with a tough decision between countries, a fall vibe can be a good clue for Finland.
Take note that this season meta is not present in Generation 2 and Generation 4 coverage.
clues.summary: A lot of the older Gen 3 coverage was filmed in autumn, so trees show fall colours. This is much rarer in the other Nordic countries, so a fall look favours Finland. Not true for Gen 2 and Gen 4.

clues.title: Landscape: lakes everywhere
text: **Lakes** are so common in Finland, that the country is also sometimes known as the Land of a Thousand Lakes. Usually, you do not have to drive long to find a body of water.
clues.summary: Lakes are so common that you rarely drive far without seeing water. The country is known as the Land of a Thousand Lakes.

clues.title: Houses: modern concrete blocks, wooden houses
text: **Finnish architecture** is mostly modern and utilitarian. Downtown areas tend to be very modern, with lots of apartment buildings and use of concrete. Suburbs mostly consist of freestanding single family homes. Many houses have wooden cladding. Like Sweden and Norway, some wooden buildings, especially in the countryside, are painted in a distinctive [dark red colour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Falu_red).
clues.summary: Mostly modern, practical buildings. Downtowns have concrete apartment blocks, and suburbs have single family homes, many with wooden cladding. Some country houses are painted dark red, like in Sweden and Norway.

clues.title: Sign: only two kinds of bus stop sign
text: Finland has two styles of **bus stop signs**, a blue and white one, and a yellow and black one.

NOTE: This can be used to tell Finland apart from Sweden, which has many different bus stop signs ([example](https://goo.gl/maps/h4BWBzQgVu4mtNgr6)), most of which have the names of the stops on them.
clues.summary: Only two bus stop sign styles: blue and white, or yellow and black. Sweden has many types, mostly with stop names written on them.

differs.how: many bus stop styles, most with stop names

clues.title: Shops: K-Market and S-Market
text: **K-Market** and **S-Market** are two Finnish supermarket chains with recognizable logos. Both chains operate only in Finland.
K-Market is sometimes known as K-Supermarket or K-Citymarket.
clues.summary: K-Market (also K-Supermarket or K-Citymarket) and S-Market are supermarket chains with recognisable logos, found only here.

clues.title: Google car: low-quality brownish camera, wide round blur
text: Google used a weird, low-quality camera in Finland. This camera is known as the **official Ari** (or “Shitcam”). It has a wide circular car blur, and can be distinguished from Generation 2 by its lack of a sky halo and often somewhat brownish colours. A good map will not usually include this coverage, but it is good to be aware of its existence, in order to not be caught off-guard by it.
NOTE: Within Europe, Finland and Spain are the countries that have the most coverage with this camera. This camera should not be confused with unofficial coverage, which is also common in Finland.
clues.summary: A rough older camera with a wide round car blur, no halo in the sky, and often brownish colours. Rare on good maps. Spain also has a lot of it, and unofficial coverage is common here.

differs.how: also has much coverage with this camera

clues.title: Google car: low-mounted camera, big round blur
text: Finland also has Generation 4 “smallcam” coverage, which is mounted lower than regular Generation 4 and has a relatively big circular blur with a small protrusion at the front. The blur can also be fully transparent, making it harder to spot.
NOTE: All of Northern Europe also has smallcam.

images.caption: Four panels labelled front panned down, front panned straight, back panned down and good blur (front)

clues.summary: A Gen 4 camera mounted lower than normal, with a fairly big round blur and a small bump at the front. The blur can be see-through, which makes it hard to spot. All Northern Europe has it.

clues.title: Route marker: first digit of 3-4 digit road number
text: Finnish regional roads have 3- or 4-digit road numbers. The **first digit** of those road numbers is **region-specific**. These regions are distributed in a rough south-to-north order, starting from 1 in the south to 9 in the north.
These road numbers often appear on direction signs. Learning the regions can help with cutting down on scanning time for 5k’s, or give you a rough region to plonk in during quick no move games.
NOTE: Major roads with 2-digit road numbers do not adhere to this geographic pattern.
clues.summary: On roads with 3 or 4 digits, the first digit shows the region, from 1 in the south to 9 in the north. Major 2-digit roads don't follow this.

clues.title: Pole: snow pole with two long reflectors
text: Snow poles which have **2 long reflectors** can be found on bigger roads in Lapland.
NOTE: They can only be found in coverage from 2023 onward.
clues.summary: Snow poles with two long reflectors are on bigger roads in the far north, only in coverage from 2023 on.

clues.title: Landscape: farmland near west and south coast
text: Finland has a lot of farmlands, but the majority of them are concentrated near the west and south coast.
clues.summary: There is a lot of farmland, but mostly near the west and south coasts.

clues.title: Landmark: wind turbines along west coast
text: **Wind turbines** are most commonly found along the **west coast** of Finland, with some exceptions.
clues.summary: Wind turbines are mostly along the west coast, with some exceptions.

clues.title: Plants: small, stunted spindly trees
text: **Small, stunted trees** with spindly, thin trunks are common in northern Finland.
clues.summary: Small stunted trees with thin spindly trunks are common in the north.

clues.title: Google car: Gen 3 snow only in the far northwest
text: **Generation 3 snow coverage **is only found in far northwestern Lapland.
NOTE: Be careful: this tip is specifically about regular Generation 3 coverage. Generation 2, 4, and trekker snow coverage can be found elsewhere.
clues.summary: Snow in older Gen 3 coverage only exists in the far northwest. Snow in Gen 2, Gen 4 and trekker coverage can be elsewhere.

clues.title: Language: Swedish text on south and west coasts
text: The **Swedish language** is common in some coastal areas in the south and the west. In these areas, bilingual Swedish or Finnish texts are common. If you see Swedish language in a Finnish setting, do not guess inland.
clues.summary: Swedish is common on some south and west coasts, often alongside Finnish. If you see Swedish in a Finnish-looking place, don't guess inland.

clues.title: Language: Sámi place names, letter c
text: The [**Sámi languages**](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A1mi_languages) are spoken in the far north of Finland. In this region, you can sometimes find bilingual signs with place names in both Finnish and Sámi. Unlike Finnish, its alphabet uses the letter **c**.
clues.summary: In the far north some signs show place names in both Finnish and Sámi. Sámi uses the letter c, which Finnish normally doesn't.

clues.title: Google car: slightly tilted long antenna
text: This slightly **tilted, long antenna** can be found in southwestern Finland.
NOTE: Do not mix it up with the straight long antenna.

images.caption: Small red circle marks the slightly tilted long antenna in the middle of the road

clues.summary: A long antenna that leans slightly, found in the southwest. Don't mix it up with the straight long antenna.

clues.title: Google car: Gen 3 with no antenna
text: Generation 3 coverage with **no antenna** at all can be found in south-central Finland.
clues.summary: Older Gen 3 coverage with no antenna at all is found in south-central areas.

clues.title: Location: island group off the southwest coast
text: **Åland** is a group of islands off the southwestern coast. It is an autonomous, mostly self-governing region of Finland with its own flag. Though it has a special status, for country streaks purposes it is still counted as part of Finland.
NOTE: Åland has no Generation 4 coverage.
clues.summary: A self-governing island group with its own flag, off the southwest coast. It counts as Finland for streaks. It has no Gen 4 coverage.

differs.how: own flag, Swedish only, short plates, dashed edge lines

clues.title: Language: only Swedish, no Finnish
text: Åland is **monolingually Swedish**. If you see only Swedish, and no Finnish language, but you suspect that you are in Finland, consider the Åland Islands.
clues.summary: If you see only Swedish and no Finnish but suspect Finland, think of the small island group in the southwest.

clues.title: Road lines: red-tinted road, dashed edge lines
text: Åland roads have two unique aspects that separate them from the rest of Finland: their pavement tends to have a **red tint**, and they have **dashed** outside road lines that resemble those found in Sweden.
clues.summary: Roads have a reddish tint and dashed edge lines like Sweden's, both unlike the rest of the country.

differs.how: Swedish roads lack the red tint

clues.title: Plate: short, almost fully white, no blue strip
text: Licence plates on Åland are white with blue text, making them appear almost completely white on Street View. They are noticeably quite **short** and **lack** the European blue strip on the left side.

images.caption: White plate on a dark car, top left

clues.summary: White plates with blue text that look almost completely white on Street View. They are short and have no European blue strip.

clues.title: Sign: pedestrian sign with 4 stripes
text: Some pedestrian signs on Åland have **four stripes**, with the exact same design found in Sweden. Beware that many pedestrian signs will still be the typical Finnish design.

images.caption: Pedestrian crossing sign with four stripes; a red arrow points to something small at the lower right

clues.summary: Some pedestrian signs have 4 stripes, exactly like Sweden's. Many are still the normal 5-stripe design.

clues.title: Bus stop: white plate with four numbers
text: Bus stops on Åland include a **white plate** with 4 numbers. Some also include this semicircle sign on top.
NOTE: Some bus stops in Mariehamn do not follow this rule.

images.caption: White bus stop plate with four numbers, on the pole in the middle

clues.summary: Bus stops show a white plate with 4 numbers, sometimes with a semicircle sign on top. Some stops in the main town don't follow this.

clues.title: Road: river valley, small stunted birch
text: **Road 970** in the far north, on the border with Norway, is easily recognizable: it runs through a river valley with hills on both sides. The river is visible in many places, usually to the northwest. The birch trees around the road are small and stunted.
NOTE: The Generation 3 coverage on this road was taken in the autumn, meaning that the vegetation looks dead and mostly devoid of leaves.

images.caption: Two roadside views labelled Gen 4 (left) and Gen 3 (right) with a number plate-style label

clues.summary: A far-northern road on the Norway border runs through a river valley with hills on both sides, a river often to the northwest and small stunted birch trees. Its Gen 3 coverage is autumn, so trees look bare.

differs.how: border road, use plates and signs to separate

clues.title: Landscape: hilly, low plants near mountains
text: Due to its proximity to the Scandinavian Mountains, the area near Kilpisjärvi features a unique **hilly **landscape, with** low vegetation**.
NOTE: [The Generation 2 coverage](https://goo.gl/maps/32NoQ1mRjDmu5CsUA) on this road was taken during Spring, so the vegetation looks dead.
clues.summary: Close to the Scandinavian Mountains the land is hilly with low plants. The Gen 2 coverage was filmed in spring, so plants look dead.

clues.title: Google car: Gen 4 sidewalk trekkers
text: Downtown Helsinki has a lot of Generation 4 **sidewalk trekker** coverage.
NOTE: This tip is specifically about Generation 4 trekker coverage. Generation 3 sidewalk trekkers can be found in many other Finnish cities.
clues.summary: The capital's downtown has a lot of Gen 4 walking-trekker coverage. Gen 3 walking trekkers exist in many other cities.

clues.title: Trams: green and yellow
text: Helsinki features these unique **green-**and-**yellow **trams.
NOTE: Tampere is the only other Finnish city with [trams](https://goo.gl/maps/zc9NtQZQvRpssehz8), but they are **red **instead of green and yellow.
clues.summary: Green and yellow trams. Only one other city has trams, and those are red.

clues.title: Buses: blue and white, vertical split
text: The buses in and around Helsinki are typically **blue-**and-**white**, with a vertical split. Buses elsewhere can have the same colour scheme, so look for one of these logos on the bus.

images.caption: A blue Finnish bus; the circles zoom in on the logos on its side

clues.summary: Buses in and around the capital are blue and white with a vertical split. Other places can have the same colours, so look for the transport company logo.

clues.title: Buses: blue bottom, white top, NYSSE
text: The buses in and around Tampere are blue on the bottom and white on the top. The word ‘NYSSE’ is written on the sides of the buses.

images.caption: A blue and white bus with NYSSE branding; the circles zoom in on the logos

clues.summary: Buses are blue on the bottom and white on top, with the word NYSSE on the sides.

clues.title: Buses: yellow with white rear
text: Buses in Turku are uniquely **yellow**, with a white rear.

images.caption: A yellow bus with a white rear; the circles zoom in on the FOLI branding

clues.summary: Yellow buses with a white rear are unique to one southwestern city.

clues.title: Buses: almost fully green
text: Buses in Jyväskylä are almost completely **green**.
clues.summary: Buses are almost completely green in one central city.

clues.title: Buses: pink front
text: Buses in Oulu have a **pink** front.
clues.summary: Buses have a pink front in one northern city.

clues.title: Plate: red metal plate with 7 golden bumps
text: You can find **Red rectangular metallic plates** with 7 golden or dark red coloured protrusions that form a rounded hexagon shape on houses, lamp posts, and signposts in Tampere.
clues.summary: Red rectangular metal plates with 7 golden or dark red bumps forming a rounded hexagon on houses, lamp posts and signposts.

clues.title: Street sign: blue with white text
text: This style of **blue street sign **with white text is unique to the cities of Seinäjoki and [Isokyrö](https://goo.gl/maps/SdmNDAwLzkXPyN6z6) southeast of Vaasa.
clues.summary: Blue street signs with white text are unique to two towns in the west, one of them Seinäjoki, southeast of Vaasa.

clues.title: Street sign: black border, all capitals
text: Lahti uses these street signs with a **black border** and all capital letters.

NOTE: You can rarely find similar signs in other cities, but Lahti almost exclusively uses this design. Notably, Kuopio can use these [signs](https://goo.gl/maps/wjdzkPYj7ba2NRGN7), which use a thicker, more compact font.
clues.summary: Signs with a black border and all capital letters are almost only used by one city. Another city uses a similar one with a thicker, more compact font.

clues.title: Street sign: blue and yellow coat of arms
text: The city of Kerava uses street signs with this **blue-**and-**yellow **[coat of arms](https://fi.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keravan_vaakuna#/media/Tiedosto:Kerava.vaakuna.svg) in the top-left corner.
clues.summary: Street signs with a blue and yellow coat of arms in the top-left corner mean one small southern city.

clues.title: Street sign: blue and grey coat of arms
text: The city of Järvenpää uses street signs with this **blue-**and-**grey **[coat of arms](https://fi.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%A4rvenp%C3%A4%C3%A4n_vaakuna#/media/Tiedosto:Jarvenpaa.vaakuna.svg) in the top-left corner. The [neighbourhood](https://media.discordapp.net/attachments/1045971390202925086/1063500707099070514/Jarvenpaan_Alueet.png) name is also written above the street name.
NOTE: If you see a street sign with a coat of arms not mentioned in this guide, you should be near Kerava or Lahti.
clues.summary: Street signs with a blue and grey coat of arms in the top-left, and the neighbourhood name above the street name, mean one small southern city.

clues.title: Sign: 5-stripe pedestrian sign, one arm up
text: **Detailed man without a hat** and **5 Zebra stripes** is Finland. Features both the detailed man's outline and the bold rounded, non-detailed person. Finland's bold non-detailed man with 5 zebra stripes has **one arm pointed up**, unlike Denmark.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: A detailed man without a hat and 5 zebra stripes. The bold simple figure has one arm pointing up, unlike Denmark's.

differs.how: Danish figure has arms pointing down

clues.title: Buses: pink Jouko brand
text: Lappeenranta has **pink** Jouko brand buses

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Pink buses of the Jouko brand mean the south-eastern city of Lappeenranta.

clues.title: Buses: LSL company
text: Lahti has an LSL bus company

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Buses run by a company called LSL mean the city of Lahti.

clues.title: Buses: Vilkku company
text: Koupio has a bus company called Vilkku.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Buses run by a company called Vilkku mean the city of Kuopio.

clues.title: Street sign: both -tie and -vägen
text: In some coastal areas of southern and western Finland, you will find bilingual signs in Finnish and Swedish. Street signs in these regions typically include both **-tie** and **-vägen** (meaning road) or both **-katu** and **-gatan** (meaning street).
NOTE: Swedish is also spoken monolingually on the Åland Islands (and in Sweden, of course).

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: In coastal parts of the south and west, signs are bilingual: both -tie and -vägen (road), or -katu and -gatan (street). Swedish alone is also spoken on the island group in the southwest.
